reason: Amethystine (Latin amethystinus) means the violet-purple of amethyst. It is a colour word, and the violet of PATO matches it.
A firm-membranaceous leaf is still membranous: thin and pliable, and 'firm' only qualifies the degree. A new intermediate term with 7 statements would not be justified.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md slot 1 (region of the bearer: apex) with docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md (reddish = approximately red PATO_0000322)
reason: This is a colour that only the tip of the part has. The quality is red on the apex of the perigynium or lobe, with an approximate-value cue, so no term is needed.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md, split into laterally compressed (PATO_0002054) + keel-shaped (PATO_0002522)
reason: Two qualities hold together: grass sheaths and lemmas are laterally compressed and keeled. Each part of the word maps to an existing PATO term.
A capitiform inflorescence has its flowers in a compact, head-like cluster. FLOPO:0991006 capitate is defined for exactly that case.
'Sub-' plus an existing value is the approximate-value pattern, as with 'suborbicular'. The value itself is FLOPO:0991287 strobiliform.
The previous review mapped channeled and channelled to PATO:0002255 grooved, so unchanneled is its negation.
Pilosulous (finely pilose) already maps to FLOPO:0991048 pilose in the candidate tables. 'Densely' is a degree modifier, not a separate quality.
Stereids are elongate, thick-walled support cells in the costa of mosses, so the word names a part, not a quality. PO has no stereid class, and sclerenchyma cell is the nearest one.
This is a transcription misspelling of poricidal, as 'anthers poricidal at the tips' shows.
A sympetalous (gamopetalous) corolla has its petals united. That is connate for like parts, read as a quality of the whole towards its parts (pattern 16).
'Obtusely' only describes the shape of the ridges, and the quality stated is ridged.
Glandular punctations are the gland dots of FLOPO:0991174 gland-dotted, so this phrase is its negation (epunctate).
Semi-spreading (French semi-étalé) means partly spreading, a value that holds only roughly. It is the approximate-value pattern on spreading, not a new term.

label: explosively dehiscent
definition: A dehiscent quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's opening suddenly and forcibly at maturity, so that its seeds are thrown away from it.
reason: Explosive dehiscence is a recognised fruit character (Impatiens, Euphorbiaceae, Acanthaceae). It is a subtype of the existing FLOPO dehiscent, alongside septicidal and loculicidal.
'In small groups' means clustered (PATO:0001629 aggregated, synonym clustered). 'Solitary or in small groups' is handled by the alternatives pattern with FLOPO:0991003 solitary.

target: docs/odp/07-alternatives.md (decreased size PATO_0000587 or medium-sized FLOPO:0991032)
reason: The slash lists two alternative size values, and each already has a term.
The word describes the scales, not the petiole or leaf: they are peltate glandular trichomes. The organ has glandular trichomes present, and those trichomes are peltate.
A hypostomatic leaf has stomata only on the abaxial surface. The informative part is that the adaxial surface has none, and PO has a class for that.
Not lustrous means not shiny, which is the positive term FLOPO:0991106 dull. A positive term is better than negating glistening.

label: rhizoid-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being long, slender, filamentous and usually unbranched and brownish, like a rhizoid.
reason: This is a resemblance quality of fern hairs, like the existing X-like classes (stolon-like, rhizome-like). It is the only term proposed here with low support (6 statements).

label: gynomonoecious
definition: A phenotypic sex quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its bearing both female flowers and bisexual flowers on the same individual.
reason: This is a standard sexual-system term (common in Asteraceae) and the counterpart of FLOPO:0991094 andromonoecious. Neither PATO nor FLOPO has it yet.

target: new: compound of two shape values (lanceolate PATO_0001877 + hastate PATO_0104352)
reason: This is a hyphenated compound of two shapes: a hastate blade with a narrowly lanceolate body. It belongs with 'oblong-ovate' compounds, not a new term.
Floras use the word in two senses: half-equitant folding for cotyledons, and enveloping for a fruiting calyx. It is too rare to pin to one quality.
Quill-shaped blades (as in quillworts and Allium) are slender and round in cross-section. Whether they are hollow is not stated, so terete is used rather than tubular.
Ruddy is a reddish colour word ('ruddy to crimson'). It could carry the approximate qualifier, as 'reddish' does.
On fruit surfaces and bark, 'slick' means smooth and even, with no projections.
Unispicate means an inflorescence made of a single spike. It is a count of parts, just as multispicate is.
Leaves, spikelets or glomerules that are densely spaced are close together on their axis, which is PATO crowded. It is the opposite of FLOPO:0991189 distant.

label: dichasial
definition: A branched quality inhering in a cymose inflorescence by virtue of two opposite lateral branches arising below each terminal flower.
reason: This is the basic cyme branching type. Its sibling FLOPO:0991327 pleiochasial already exists, and FLOPO:0991255 cyme-like does not say how the cyme branches.
